title: Personal Blog
description: Personal blog backend developed with Spring Boot, featuring user authentication, post management, and a RESTful API for frontend consumption.

details.intro: Spring Boot backend following best practices with a modular layered architecture, DTOs for clean API contracts, pagination support for large datasets, secure authentication and authorization, well-separated modules and services, comprehensive unit and integration tests, and full Swagger/OpenAPI documentation for the REST API. The backend is designed to be consumed by a frontend application, providing endpoints for user registration, login, post creation, editing, deletion, and retrieval with pagination.

title: Prok
description: Full-featured To-Do list web application with authentication and task management, built using Spring Boot and Thymeleaf.

details.intro: Prok is a personal task management application designed to help users organize their daily activities. The platform allows users to register, log in, and manage their tasks through an intuitive web interface built with Thymeleaf. Each user has their own private task list, with features for creating, editing, completing, and deleting tasks. The backend is powered by Spring Boot and follows the MVC pattern, ensuring clean separation between business logic, data handling, and presentation.

steps.stepDesc: Defined the main features: secure user authentication, private task lists, and task CRUD operations.
Applied the MVC pattern with Spring Boot, separating controllers, services, and repositories for maintainability.
Designed a relational schema in PostgreSQL with separate tables for users and tasks, linked through foreign keys.
Integrated Spring Security with session-based authentication to protect user data and restrict access to private task lists.
Developed responsive HTML templates with Thymeleaf for dynamic rendering of tasks, forms, and user data.
Implemented create, read, update, and delete operations for tasks, as well as the ability to mark tasks as completed.
Applied CSS for a clean, user-friendly interface, ensuring mobile responsiveness.
Used Docker to containerize the application and database for easier deployment and testing.
Performed manual testing to ensure correctness of authentication, task operations, and UI rendering.

title: Microservices System for Web Architectures
description: Final project of Web Architectures subject, developed as a team, with planning and design of a microservices architecture solution in Java and Spring Boot, integrated with PostgreSQL and MongoDB.

details.intro: In this project, we needed to create a program that allows people to rent electric skateboards. Basically, the user selects one of the predefined stops in the city (this will be the pickup point for the skateboard). The user also decides when to end the ride. When this happens, he/she needs to select another predefined stop in the city to leave the skateboard, and then the total cost is charged to the user's account.

steps.stepDesc: We defined the main system features, including user management, skateboard management, and trips.
We designed a basic microservices architecture that included a user service, a trip service, and a skateboard management service.
We used PostgreSQL and MongoDB to store data related to users, accounts, and trips. The necessary tables and their relationships were defined.
We created REST APIs using Spring Boot for each microservice, enabling interaction between users and the system.
We implemented a GPS simulation using coordinates (x, y) for the stops and skateboards. A simple if condition was used to check if the skateboard was at a stop to allow trip completion.
We developed key features such as account creation, trip start and end, and cost calculation.
We used Docker to containerize the microservices, making deployment and execution easier across different environments.
We performed basic manual tests to verify the correct operation of the APIs and system logic.

title: Game Sphere
description: Final project for the User Interfaces subject, developed as a team. The project involved the design and implementation of a minigames page, where we applied UI/UX design principles.

details.intro: In this project, we aimed to create a web platform for playing online minigames. The main idea was to design an intuitive and visually appealing page that followed UX and UI principles to ensure a smooth user experience. The platform allows users to explore different minigames through a clean, structured layout. Additionally, we developed an interactive 4 in a Line game, where two players can compete by placing pieces on a grid, with the objective of connecting four in a row to win. Every design decision was guided by user-centered thinking, from creating prototypes in Figma to ensuring responsiveness and interactivity with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

steps.stepDesc: We started by identifying the target audience and defining key requirements for the minigames page. The goal was to create a platform that offered simplicity, fun, and ease of use.

Using Figma, we created interactive prototypes and detailed designs for the minigames page. This helped us visualize the final product and define a consistent style guide (colors, typography, and spacing) before starting the implementation.
We translated the Figma prototypes into semantic HTML, ensuring the structure of the page was accessible and well-organized.
With the designs from Figma as a guide, we used CSS to style the website, focusing on creating an engaging and responsive user experience.

We implemented interactive features with JavaScript, such as Navigation between different sections of the minigames page, Dynamic content loading for game categories and games and Basic animations to improve user engagement.

steps.stepTitle: Developing the Minigame: 4 in a Line
steps.stepDesc: We programmed the 4 in a Line game, focusing on providing a fun and intuitive gameplay experience.
After completing the first version, we conducted user testing to gather feedback on the usability and design. This helped us refine both the UI and the gameplay.
Once all adjustments were made, we finalized the project and prepared it for presentation, ensuring it met all the project requirements.

title: Fragantica
description: Final project for the Web 2 course, developed independently. The project involved designing and implementing a RESTful application using PHP, with the API consumed on the frontend.

details.intro: In this project, I developed a catalog of perfumes with authentication and an administration panel. The goal was to build a complete web application with a PHP backend, a template engine for the front end, and Bootstrap for styling. The system allows regular users to view the catalog and an admin user to manage perfumes (add, update, or delete). To achieve this, I implemented a custom router in PHP to handle different routes dynamically and created a simple authentication system to manage user access. The project also included database design and interaction using MariaDB for data storage.

steps.stepDesc: Defined the main features of the catalog, including user roles (regular user and admin), perfume management, and authentication.
Designed the database schema using MariaDB. It included tables for perfumes and users, with appropriate relationships and fields to support CRUD operations.
Developed a custom PHP router to manage dynamic routing for the different pages (home, perfume details, admin panel). Added route guards to ensure only admins could access the management panel.
Created a simple authentication system where users can log in, and admins have additional privileges to manage the perfume catalog.
Used a PHP template engine combined with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap to create a responsive and user-friendly UI for the catalog and admin panel.
Implemented functionalities for the admin user to add new perfumes, update existing ones, and delete them from the database.
Performed manual testing to verify that all routes worked correctly, user roles were respected, and database operations (CRUD) were functioning as expected.
